schema.title: Response List Templates Diagram Templates Get

post.description:
Build a diagram from a template.

Each slot is bound to an existing element of its type, to an element to
create, or left out. Everything refusable is refused before anything is
written; relationships are created only if `create_relationships` is true.

get.description: Every saved diagram, sorted by name — or only those filed in a package.

post.description: A new, empty diagram. Its name must not be taken.

A new **live** view: everything a saved query or a package yields, at each opening.

It stores no box. To edit it, freeze it; to see it frozen from the start,
freeze it right after (the layout is the SPA's, the server computes none).

delete.description: Delete a diagram. The elements it showed are untouched.

get.description:
A diagram with its boxes, the elements they show and the links between them.

`as_of` removes nothing: it lists, in `inactive_*_ids`, what is out of period that day.

anyOf.description: Read the model as it is on this day (YYYY-MM-DD): what is not in service that day is left out. Leave it out for no date filter.

post.description: Keep the shape of a diagram: each element becomes a slot of the same type.
Store the layout and make the live view an ordinary editable diagram.

put.description:
Replace the whole scene of a diagram at once.

`revision` is the one the client read; if somebody saved since, nothing is
written and the answer is a 409 `diagram_revision_conflict`. Otherwise the
new revision comes back in `X-Diagram-Revision`. Each element must exist
and appear once, and a route may only name a link joining two placed
elements; otherwise nothing is written.

get.description: The one static drawing of a diagram, cacheable by content (`ETag`).

200.description: The diagram as a static SVG (docs/adr/0063).

get.description: What a frozen view would gain and lose if it followed its source again. Writes nothing.

post.description:
Back to a live view. Refused (409) while notes, groups or routes would be lost,
unless `discard_annotations` is true.

get.description: One document with its markdown, as text.

put.description:
Replace the content of a document with a newer version of the same file.

The uploaded name must match the stored one: a document is known to its
readers by its name, so overwriting `runbook.md` with something else under
that name is refused rather than silently accepted.

get.description:
The document as a safe HTML fragment, for a reader that cannot render markdown.

Raw HTML in the document is shown as text, images are not loaded and `javascript:` / `data:`
links are not links (docs/adr/0062): the SPA inserts the result with `v-html` for exactly
that reason.

Browse the catalogue, narrowed by type, by layer, by a name fragment
or filed in a package (subpackages included unless told otherwise).

anyOf.description: Read the model as it is on this day (YYYY-MM-DD): what is not in service that day is left out. Leave it out for no date filter.

post.description: Add an element to the catalogue.
File up to 100 elements in a package, or at the root; all or none.

Types, layers, name fragment, package, attributes and links present or absent.

Every criterion is combined with AND. `total` counts everything the query
matches, not the page. Reading needs no more than a login — it is a read.

delete.description: Remove an element and every relationship attached to it.

patch.description: Change what an element says. Its type is fixed once created.

post.description:
Move an element through review.

403 without the role the token carries, 409 if the state forbids it or if
`expected_revision` is no longer the element's revision.

get.description:
What is attached to an element: the names and the sizes, not the text.

A 404 rather than an empty list when the element is unknown — an empty list
is the answer to a different question.

schema.title: Response List Element Documents Elements  Element Id  Documents Get

post.description:
Attach a markdown file to an element.

The element must already exist, and it may hold only one document under a

`EA_EXCHANGE_MAX_EXPORTS` are prepared or sent at once (429 and `Retry-After` beyond).

post.description:
Simulate (the default) or apply an exchange file; editors only, simulation included.

Writing needs `dry_run=false`, said outright: a client that forgets destroys nothing.
To confirm, send the same file(s) again with `dry_run=false`; the report's `sha256` says
it is what was simulated. The import is idempotent (an existing element or link is
reused), so a client whose connection was cut can send it again. XML takes `file`; CSV
takes `elements` and, optionally, `relations` and `properties` — three files, never an
archive. The ceiling is on their sum. Neither a file's name nor its declared type is read.
